rejections.question: How many of our accounts have no country recorded?
How many of our subscriptions use plans that have been retired from sale?
rejections.notes: “Our subscriptions” could mean all subscription records or only subscriptions currently in use; the query counts every status, including canceled subscriptions. Specify whether to include canceled subscriptions (or say “active subscriptions” if that is intended).

rejections.question: For tickets opened in 2025, how many were assigned to each member of the Support team, and what was their average customer satisfaction score, ignoring unanswered surveys and rounded to two decimals? Include only people assigned at least two of those tickets.
rejections.notes: “Support team” could mean users whose team has the name Support or users in the support department; the schema distinguishes teams.name from teams.department. The SQL filters LOWER(T2.name) = 'support', so it misses support-department members whose team has another name. Clarify which is intended; if it means the department, filter LOWER(T2.department) = 'support'.

rejections.question: For each plan tier, how many active subscriptions and licensed seats does Parker Health have? Include only tiers with active subscriptions.
rejections.notes: The question asks for each tier's count of active subscriptions and total licensed seats for Parker Health, but the SQL only looks up the account name. Join accounts to subscriptions and plans, filter to Parker Health and active subscriptions, then group by plan tier and return the subscription count and seat sum.

rejections.question: For each agent on the Support team with tickets opened in Q2 2026, how many tickets were opened and what was the average recorded satisfaction score, excluding unanswered surveys and rounded to two decimals?
rejections.notes: “Support team” could mean a team whose name is Support or users in the support department; the schema distinguishes teams.name from teams.department and gives examples of regional team names. “Agent” could also mean users with role='support_agent'. The SQL filters only LOWER(teams.name)='support' and does not filter the department or role, so it may include or omit the wrong users. Specify the intended team criterion and whether the support_agent role is required, then filter accordingly.

rejections.question: For Matthew Cook's deals actually won in 2025, what was the average deal value in each deal currency? Show up to 20 currencies in alphabetical currency-code order, with averages rounded to two decimals.
rejections.notes: The SQL searches users for names containing “matthew”; it does not identify Matthew Cook’s deals, filter for deals actually won in 2025, or calculate average deal amounts by currency. Join users to deals, match Matthew Cook, filter won deals by closed_at in 2025, and group the average amount by deal currency. The result rows are user names, not the requested averages.

rejections.question: For active subscriptions managed by Alyssa Curry, how many seats are there in each plan tier, and what is the average subscription discount in each tier, counting every subscription equally? Round discount percentages to two decimals.
For each Support team agent with tickets opened in Q2 2026, how many of those tickets were resolved by the end of 2026-09-30? Include agents with zero resolved tickets and former employees.
rejections.notes: The query filters `LOWER(T2.name) = 'support'`, but the schema identifies a team's department with `teams.department` (whose value is `support`). Filter on `T2.department = 'support'` so it includes agents on Support-department teams regardless of their team names.

rejections.question: For each month of 2025 with tickets opened by Peterson-Anderson, how many tickets were opened and how many of those received a satisfaction rating? Match the account name without regard to capitalization.
For each plan tier, how many active subscriptions does Anthony Shields manage, and how many licensed seats do those subscriptions have? Include only tiers where he manages active subscriptions.

For each month from January through September 2026, what was the average number of days from creation to actual close for deals we won, grouped by the month they closed? Include partial days and round averages to two decimals.
rejections.notes: “For each month from January through September” could mean all nine calendar months, but the SQL returns only months containing won deals (the result has only August). Clarify that only months with won deals should be shown, or generate all nine months and return NULL for months with no qualifying deals. The date-difference calculation and grouping otherwise match the request.

rejections.question: Which 10 accounts had the highest average resolution time for tickets resolved between 2026-01-01 and 2026-09-30, considering only accounts with at least three such tickets? Show the account, ticket count and average elapsed hours rounded to two decimals. Break ties by account ID.
rejections.notes: The tie-break direction is unspecified; clarify whether account ID should be ascending or descending. The SQL uses ascending account ID.

rejections.question: For each month from January through September 2026, what was the average number of calendar days from a contact being added to their first logged call, email, meeting or demo? Group by the month the contact was added, consider only contacts added in that period who had such an activity by 2026-09-30, and round averages to two decimals.
rejections.notes: The SQL can select an activity that occurred before the contact was added, producing a negative interval instead of finding the first matching activity after creation. Add a lower-bound condition such as T2.occurred_at >= T1.created_at before taking MIN().

rejections.question: Which 10 accounts owned by Jason Frazier had gone the longest without a logged call, email, meeting or demo as of 2026-09-30? Include only accounts with at least one such activity by that date. Show the account, most recent qualifying activity date and whole calendar days since that activity. Break ties by account ID.
rejections.notes: The SQL only looks up a matching user name; it does not find Jason Frazier’s accounts or their qualifying activities, calculate the latest activity date or days elapsed, or return the 10 longest-inactive accounts in the requested order. Rewrite it to join Jason’s user record to owned accounts and qualifying activities through 2026-09-30, aggregate each account’s latest activity, calculate whole calendar days since that date, and order by days descending then account ID ascending before limiting to 10. The result contains only Jason Frazier’s name, not the requested columns.

rejections.question: Which 10 accounts with at least one urgent support ticket opened in Q3 2026 paid us the most in successful payments during that quarter? Show each account's collected total in USD using our fixed reporting rates, rounded to two decimals, and break ties by account ID.

Which 10 deals actually won in 2025 had the highest USD values and at least one demo logged against them before they closed? Show the deal, account, sales rep, and value converted using our fixed reporting rates, rounded to two decimals. Break ties by deal ID.

For invoices issued in 2025, which 10 have the largest difference between their subtotal and the sum of their line amounts, counting invoices with no lines as having a line sum of zero? Rank by the absolute difference converted to USD using the fixed reporting rates, and show the invoice number and signed difference in USD, rounded to two decimals. Break ties by invoice ID.
rejections.notes: The requested signed difference has no explicit sign convention: it could be subtotal minus line sum or line sum minus subtotal. The SQL uses subtotal minus line sum. Specify that direction in the question; then the SQL matches it.

rejections.question: Which 10 users in the Support team have never logged in? Include inactive users, show each person's name and manager's name, and order by user ID.
For each plan with active subscriptions, how many active subscriptions and licensed seats do we have, and what is their average subscription discount percentage, rounded to two decimals?

For each payment method used in 2026-01-01 through 2026-09-30, how many successful payments did we receive and what was the average successful payment amount by currency, in major currency units rounded to two decimals?
rejections.notes: “For each payment method” can ask for a count aggregated across currencies, while “by currency” may apply only to the average. The SQL instead reports both count and average for each method-currency pair. Clarify that both metrics should be grouped by method and currency, or specify that the count should be a method-level total.

rejections.question: Show the line descriptions and quantities on Brightpath Learning's invoices issued in September 2026. Return up to 20 lines, ordered by invoice number and then line item ID.
rejections.notes: The SQL only looks up an account name; it does not retrieve invoice line descriptions or quantities, join invoices and line items, filter invoices issued in September 2026, or order by invoice number and line item ID. Replace it with a query joining accounts to invoices and invoice_line_items, filtering the account and issue-date range, and selecting the requested columns in the specified order.

rejections.question: Show the 10 most recent failed payment attempts in September 2026, with their invoice numbers, payment methods and attempted amounts in major currency units, rounded to two decimals. Include the currency and break ties by payment ID, lowest first.

For each account manager, how many of their accounts have a primary contact whose job title is Chief Financial Officer? Ignore capitalization and surrounding spaces in the title. Show only managers with matches, ordered by manager ID, limited to 20 managers.
For each quarter from Q1 through Q3 2026, how many urgent tickets were opened without a contact recorded? Ignore capitalization in urgency labels and include only quarters with matching tickets.
How many accounts did we add in 2025?
Show our 10 most recently issued open invoices, with invoice number, issue date and currency. Break ties by invoice number.
rejections.notes: “Break ties by invoice number” does not specify ascending or descending order. The gold SQL assumes ascending; because the 10-row limit can split invoices with the same issue date, this may change which invoices are returned. Specify the tie-break direction.

rejections.question: How many of our accounts are currently customers, regardless of how the stage is capitalized?
How many contacts have the job title 'Chief Financial Officer', ignoring capitalization and spaces at the start or end?
How many deals created in 2026 have a USD value above the average value of our USD deals created in 2026?
rejections.notes: “USD value” could mean the deal amount converted to USD, while “USD deals” could mean deals denominated in USD. The SQL counts only USD-denominated deals and compares their unconverted amounts, so it does not answer the converted-value reading. Clarify whether to include deals in other currencies and, if so, specify the comparison population; convert amounts using currencies.usd_rate as needed. The hard label fits the aggregate comparison (and currency conversion, if intended).

rejections.question: How much did we collect through successful EUR payments each month in Q2 2026, in euros rounded to two decimals?
rejections.notes: “Each month in Q2” could mean all three calendar months, including a month with no successful EUR payments, or only months with payments. The grouped query omits zero-payment months (tenant 2 has no May row). Clarify that only months with payments should be shown, or generate all three months and return 0.00 for months with none.

rejections.question: What were our total invoice charges and total tax on non-void EUR invoices issued in 2025, rounded to two decimals?
rejections.notes: “Total invoice charges” could mean the subtotal before tax or the total_amount payable including tax. The SQL sums total_amount, so it does not return the subtotal if that is what “charges” means. Specify either “subtotal before tax” and sum subtotal, or “total amount payable, including tax” and sum total_amount.

rejections.question: For each month from January through September 2026, what were the total charges and tax on our non-void EUR invoices issued that month, rounded to two decimals? Only include months with matching invoices.
rejections.notes: “Total charges” could mean the pre-tax subtotal or the amount payable including tax. The SQL sums total_amount (which already includes tax) and tax; specify whether the requested charges are subtotal or total_amount, then sum the corresponding column and tax. The query is a straightforward one-table monthly aggregation with no described data trap, so easy fits better than medium.

rejections.question: For deals actually won in 2025, what was our total EUR deal value by lead source, including unknown sources as a separate group, rounded to two decimals?
rejections.notes: “EUR deal value” could mean either deals denominated in EUR or all deal values converted to EUR; these yield different results. The SQL only includes EUR-denominated deals. Clarify the intended meaning; if conversion is intended, convert amounts to EUR rather than filtering on currency_code. The medium label is appropriate for the grouped aggregation.

rejections.question: Which 10 currently open invoices were the most days overdue on 2026-09-30? Include only invoices due before that date, show the invoice number, account name and whole days overdue, and break ties by invoice ID.

How many of our invoices issued in 2025 had due dates that fell on observed US federal holidays?

The explanation therefore gives no valid reason to abstain. The hard label is not appropriate for recognizing unanswerability because this question is answerable.

How many support tickets were opened on Ontario statutory holidays in 2025?
rejections.notes: The standard Ontario statutory holidays for 2025 can be listed as date literals and matched against ticket opening dates, so the missing calendar table does not make this unanswerable. The probe also has a malformed Boxing Day date (`2025-12-26 تش`), so its query may omit tickets opened that day. Medium is a reasonable difficulty for recognizing the missing-calendar trap, but the item should not be labeled unanswerable.
